newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE official says foreign troops in Gulf essential.
newsitem.headline: UAE official says foreign troops in Gulf essential.

text.p: Foreign troops deployed in the oil-rich Gulf are essential to preserve the region's security, the United Arab Emirates foreign minister said on Saturday.

"The presence of foreign troops is an important element to consolidate security and stability in a region that has witnessed two wars in 15 years," the state-owned Emirates News Agency quoted Rashid Abdullah Al-Nuaimi as telling journalists in Abu Dhabi.
The foreign military presence in the Gulf since a U.S.-led coalition drove Iraqi troops from Kuwait in 1991 has been criticised by opposition groups and Iran.
There are some 20,000 U.S. troops and 300 warplanes deployed in and around the Gulf, with some forces and aircraft based in Saudi Arabia and Kuwait.
Coalition troops including British and French forces are based in Saudi Arabia to enforce a "no-fly zone" for Iraqi planes over southern Iraq.

United States and British warships are deployed in the Gulf waterway as part of a multinational effort enforcing U.N. sanctions on Iraq. The U.S forces also keep a close watch on Iran's military moves.
